model: FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route): adjusted continuing-ops earnings less capital retention, net debt held at zero

inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2025 cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments expense' R$297,022k (FY2024 R$232,672k; FY2023 R$251,239k). EquityAwardTaxes disclosed as 0 in kpis. Adjusted net income has NOT excluded SBC since March 2023 (20-F FY2025 selected-data note (c)), so the adjusted-earnings base used here is already SBC-expensed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow R$2,987.0m for 40.29m shares at R$75.98 avg (20-F treasury-share movement table). 1Q26 R$531.8m, 2Q26 R$739.0m (2Q26 release Table 13). The flat diluted count is being funded in cash; buybacks are value-neutral in this model because SBC is expensed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, 30-Jun-2026 estimate: 243.2m basic at 31-Mar-2026 (20-F FY2025 p.8145: 229,177,062 Class A + 14,051,164 Class B, ex-treasury -- confirmed by R$3.08bn dividend / US$2.53 / 243.2m = USDBRL 5.00) less ~12m repurchased in 2Q26 (R$739m at ~R$60/share) = ~231m basic, plus 6.6m dilutive share-based instruments under IAS 33 treasury-stock method (20-F note 16.3.1) = 237.6m. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so grant dilution is already charged. 1 Nasdaq share = 1 Class A common share (no ADS ratio). Note: Metrics.csv FY2025 SharesOutstanding 273.5m is the FY2025 diluted weighted average (note 16.3), not a period-end count.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all driver paths in BRL; Nasdaq quote in USD. fx_rate is USD per BRL = 1/5.2223 (Yahoo BRL=X regularMarketPrice 5.2223 at 2026-10-03T09:58Z). Parity check: the April-2026 extraordinary dividend of US$2.53/share totalled R$3.08bn on 243.2m shares = R$12.66/share, implying USDBRL 5.00 at the April-2026 record date, consistent with the direction and the share basis. No dual listing exists (Class A shares trade directly on Nasdaq, 1:1, no ADS). A USD investor also bears BRL drift: the 10-year average depreciation has been ~4-5%/yr; the hurdle rate below is lifted to carry the inflation-differential portion of that.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is a BRL COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: the flows are post-interest FCFE. Build: normalised Brazil 10-year nominal government yield 12.0% (NTN-F traded ~13.5-14% through 2025-26 at the Selic peak of 14-15%; CDI was 14.4% in 2Q26 and management's own 2026 plan assumed ~12.5%), equity risk premium 5.5%, local-market beta 1.0 => 17.5% nominal BRL. No ad-hoc premium for credit-cycle, competition or FX risk: those are charged once, in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight. Same rate in all three scenarios. Equivalent USD cost of equity ~14.5% after the ~3pp BRL/USD inflation differential. Terminal growth 5.0% nominal BRL = ~3.5% inflation (BCB target 3% +/-1.5) + ~1.5% real; bear 4.0%.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: lease payments (principal R$79.7m FY2025 + interest) sit inside cost of services / financial expenses in the adjusted P&L the EBITDA path is built from, and lease liabilities are excluded from the (zero) net-debt bridge. Charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI immaterial (R$42.3m equity at 30-Jun-2026; R$16.4m of FY2025 continuing profit). Adjusted net income used as the earnings anchor is attributable to controlling shareholders, so no bridge deduction -- charged once.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. StoneCo is a payments acquirer that has become a balance-sheet financial: 74% of revenue is financial income (prepayment of merchant receivables, credit book, float) funded by R$17.6bn of borrowings/institutional deposits, R$10.8bn of retail deposits and R$17.6bn of payables to clients; the credit portfolio is R$3.75bn and growing >100% YoY; it is regulated as a prudential conglomerate with a 26.3% Tier-1 ratio. Reported OCF-minus-capex (FY2024 -R$4.9bn, FY2025 -R$0.5bn) is receivables-funding noise, and deducting the funding stack as 'net debt' from an enterprise value would be a category error (dcf-methods SKILL.md: deposits are not net debt; never FCF/WACC on a post-interest flow). The business therefore straddles the operating-company and bank rows; rather than sum two parts that share one funding stack, the whole is valued as a financial: FCFE = adjusted continuing-ops net income (after all funding cost, provisions and SBC) + D&A - capex - capital retained for growth, capitalised at a BRL cost of equity, net debt held at zero. ENGINE MAPPING: 'ebitda_margin_path' = (adjusted EBT + D&A + SBC) / revenue, so that EBIT after the engine's SBC and D&A charges equals adjusted pre-tax profit (FY2025: 2,903.2 + 912.4 + 297.0 = 4,112.6 / 14,153.8 = 29.1%; FY2024 30.0%; 1H26 27.5%). 'cash_tax_rate_path' is the adjusted effective tax rate (FY2025 14.7%, 1H26 15.4%) ramped toward 20% as Pillar-2 and Brazilian reform erode the low-rate entities. 'wc_capture_pct' of -40 is NOT working capital: it is the capital-retention proxy -- RWA R$19.8bn grew ~8% (R$1.6bn) in the year to 2Q26, and holding a ~18% managerial Tier-1 ratio on that growth retains ~R$290m/yr, which is ~40% of the ~R$700m annual revenue increase; it scales with growth in each scenario as retention should. Capex includes intangibles (software) development. EXCLUDED-INCOME RULE: adjusted net cash (R$1,350m at 30-Jun-2026, company definition) and the ~R$2bn of regulatory capital above a 15% ratio are NOT added in the bridge because their yield (other financial income R$900m+/yr) stays in the flows -- asset and income are on the same side. last_fcf is the FY2025 FCFE proxy (2,477.2 adj NI + 912.4 D&A - ~1,100 continuing capex - 0.4 x 2,104 revenue increase = ~1,448); reported_fcf is OCF - capex as reported and is not meaningful for this business, so the owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does not hold on this route. interest_income is 0 because nothing is stripped. BASE REVENUE is FY2025 continuing operations (Linx classified as discontinued; FY2023-25 continuing 10,761.1 / 12,049.6 / 14,153.8). HURDLE: entry_price.hurdle_rate is 0.18 in BRL = the house 15% USD hurdle plus ~3pp BRL/USD inflation differential; a 15% BRL IRR would be below the 17.5% cost of equity and would put the 'entry price' above intrinsic value. GUIDANCE ANCHOR: FY2026 adjusted basic EPS guided R$10.80-11.40, management steering to the low end (2Q26 call); base FY2026 adjusted net income ~R$2.44bn sits ~4% below the low end because 15-90d NPL went 2.51% -> 6.00% and >90d 4.67% -> 8.60% in a year while coverage fell to 204%.

balance_sheet_memo.treatment: Funding stack is operating, not net debt; net_debt set to 0 and no surplus-capital bridge item (see notes).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year average nominal BRL revenue growth (4% FY2026 rising to 8% then fading to 5%); the primary house choice, equity CAGR, is negative and unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-5.8% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+33.6%) and EPS (+23.9%) by far more than 30% because R$4.9bn of buybacks (FY2024-25) and the R$3.6bn Linx goodwill impairment (4Q24) shrank book value while the business grew; book-value compounding is not the economic driver of a buyback-funded financial. Revenue 3yr CAGR mixes an FY2022 base that includes Linx software (~R$1.3bn) against a continuing-ops FY2025, so it understates; the continuing-only 2yr CAGR is 14.7% but half of that was CDI-driven financial income which reverses as rates fall. EPS 3yr CAGR is null because FY2022 EPS was negative (-1.67). FCF CAGRs are null: reported FCF is receivables-funding noise (FY2021 +2.3bn, FY2024 -4.9bn).
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted FCF series not meaningful for this business (see inputs.notes); SBC has been a stable 2.0-2.4% of revenue since FY2022, so it is not outgrowing earnings.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +4% (1H26 +4.4% YoY; transaction revenue -31% on MDR-to-prepayment repricing, financial income +11%, credit revenue +166%). FY2027-29 7-8% as the credit book (R$3.75bn, +107% YoY) keeps compounding off a small base and TPV recovers to mid-single digits after the Ton churn fix; fades to 5% nominal (= ~1.5% real) as acquiring matures and Pix QR cannibalises card TPV. All nominal BRL.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 29.1%, 1H26 27.5% (provisions 4.9% of revenue vs 2.4% a year earlier). FY2026 28.2% assumes 2H seasonality and the CDI easing from 14.4%; recovery to 29.0% by FY2030 as cost of risk falls from 21.5% to high-teens (guided) and funding mix shifts to deposits, capped there because take-rate competition from bank-owned acquirers and Nubank/Mercado Pago absorbs the operating leverage. Never regains FY2024's 30.0%.
base.tax_rationale: Adjusted ETR 14.7% FY2025 / 15.4% 1H26, below the 34% statutory because of entities taxed at different rates and interest-on-equity deductions; Pillar-2 QDMTT (15% floor on Brazilian entities from 2025) and reform risk ramp it to 20% by FY2031.
base.capital_retention_rationale: wc_capture_pct -40: ~R$290m/yr retained for RWA growth at an ~18% Tier-1 ratio against ~R$700m/yr revenue growth (see inputs.notes).
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 17.5%-5.0% = 8.4x terminal FCFE; cap of 12x does not bind. The stock trades at ~4.6x FY2026 guided adjusted EPS, so the terminal multiple assumes re-rating only to a single-digit earnings multiple.

bull.rationale: Credit and banking cross-sell lift ARPAC through the 4.8m client base; cost of risk normalises to mid-teens as government-backed lines mix in and 2H25 vintages season; Selic falls to 11-12% cutting financial expenses (30% of revenue) and reviving SMB credit demand; margin regains and exceeds FY2024's 30.0% by FY2030. Tax stays nearer today's 15-16% as the low-rate structures persist.

bear.rationale: A smaller replay of 2021: the 2H25/1H26 vintages and 'dedicated desk' large-ticket loans push cost of risk to 25-30% on a R$4-5bn book (R$1.0-1.4bn of provisions vs R$0.7bn run-rate), management freezes credit growth, and Selic stays 14%+ through 2027. Card TPV keeps shrinking (-3% YoY in 2Q26) as Pix QR and bank-owned acquirers take share; revenue is flat nominal (falling real) for three years. Margin troughs at 24% in FY2028 and settles at 25%, 4pp below FY2025. Tax drifts to 22%, terminal growth 4% nominal.

scenario_narratives.base: Stone is a mature Brazilian acquirer bolting a young merchant-credit book onto a deposit-funded balance sheet. The base case takes management's FY2026 EPS guidance at slightly below its low end, lets the credit book keep compounding at a slowing pace with cost of risk easing from 21.5% toward the high-teens management has guided, and assumes CDI falls from 14.4% over 2026-27 so financial expenses stop absorbing 30% of revenue. Take-rate compression (transaction revenue -31% YoY) continues to be re-captured in financial income. Margin recovers to, but never above, 29%; growth fades to 5% nominal. The valuation is a single-digit earnings multiple on a flat-to-modestly-growing earnings stream, with the flat diluted share count funded by continuing R$2-3bn/yr buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: Three things go right together: the Selic cycle turns (11-12% by 2027), cost of risk normalises as government-backed lines and seasoned vintages dominate the book, and the Ton churn fix holds so TPV re-accelerates to high single digits. Credit then becomes the ARPAC engine management promised, ROE holds above 20% on a smaller equity base, and margin exceeds FY2024's 30%. Requires all three; hence the 20% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2Q26 credit data is the warning, not the peak: NPL 15-90d tripled and >90d nearly doubled in a year while coverage fell 76pp, in only the book's second year of hypergrowth, with a dedicated-desk concentration problem on top. In this case losses in 2H26-2027 force a credit retrenchment just as the acquiring core loses share to Pix and bank-owned acquirers, and Selic stays higher for longer. Revenue is flat nominal for three years, margin troughs at 24%, and the equity base keeps shrinking through buybacks at a time it should be rebuilt. Weighted 30%: the balance sheet survives (26% Tier-1 ratio, R$1.35bn adjusted net cash), but the company has done this before (2021) and the stock is pricing roughly this outcome today.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the thesis rests on an unproven credit-underwriting pivot (book +107% YoY while 15-90d NPL went 2.51% -> 6.00% and coverage fell to 204%), the company has a 2021 precedent of a credit write-down that halved the stock, and management is already guiding to the low end on a higher-for-longer Selic. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs three independent things (rate cuts, credit normalisation, churn fix) to land together. Base 50%.

entry_price.hurdle_note: 18% in BRL = the house 15% USD hurdle plus ~3pp expected BRL/USD depreciation from the inflation differential (BCB target 3% vs Fed 2%, plus Brazil's historical real-depreciation drift). A 15% BRL hurdle would sit below the 17.5% BRL cost of equity and put the entry price above intrinsic value, which is not what the house entry price means.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Stone as what it has become -- a deposit- and debt-funded merchant financial -- not as a software-like payments company: capitalise fully-SBC-expensed, post-funding-cost, post-provision adjusted earnings less the capital the balance sheet must retain to grow, at a Brazilian-real cost of equity, with the credit cycle charged in the scenario weights rather than in an inflated discount rate. The surplus capital and adjusted net cash are left in the flows (their yield is in revenue) rather than added to the bridge, which is the conservative side of the matching rule. The output is an earnings multiple: the base case capitalises FY2026 FCFE at ~9x, against a market paying ~4.6x guided EPS.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit-book losses: a cost of risk of 25-30% on a R$4-5bn book would remove R$0.5-0.8bn of pre-tax profit, roughly the whole gap between the base and bear margins; the 2021 collateral/credit episode shows Stone's underwriting edge has failed once before.
Selic/CDI path: financial expenses are 30% of revenue and CDI-linked; each 100bp of CDI held longer is roughly R$300m of annual gross profit per management's 2026 commentary.
BRL/USD: every per-share value here is converted at spot 5.22; the 10-year BRL depreciation trend is 4-5%/yr and the USD IV scales one-for-one with the rate.
Take-rate and share erosion: card TPV fell 3% YoY in 2Q26; Pix QR (+44%) carries lower economics, and bank-owned acquirers can cross-subsidise MDR.
Tax: the adjusted ETR of 15% depends on entity structures that Pillar-2 and Brazilian tax reform are eroding; every 5pp is ~R$150m of net income.

Share-count basis: the 30-Jun-2026 count is estimated from the 31-Mar-2026 20-F figure and 2Q26 buyback cash; the 3Q26 release will give the actual and 3Q26 buybacks will have lowered it further (which raises per-share value).

Capital-retention proxy: -40% of incremental revenue is a judgment on the RWA growth / Tier-1 ratio relationship; if Stone runs the ratio down toward 15% instead, retention is lower and value higher, and vice versa in a credit stress.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, STNE regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 8.95-19.64. FX: Yahoo BRL=X at the time stated in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: STNE_Metrics.csv (continuing-ops revenue FY2023-25); 20-F FY2025 (adjusted net income continuing R$2,477.2m / 2,108.2m / 1,437.2m FY2025/24/23; D&A continuing R$912.4m note 10.4; SBC R$297.0m; EPS note 16.3; treasury-share table; share counts at 31-Dec-2025 and 31-Mar-2026); 2Q26 earnings release 13-Aug-2026 (adjusted P&L, credit and banking KPIs, cash flow, balance sheet, adjusted net cash, capital ratio); 4Q25 release (quarterly adjusted EBT for FY2025, adjusted net cash R$2,588.1m).
data_sources.qualitative: STNE_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): business model, credit-quality trend, FY2026 guidance (adjusted gross profit R$6.6-7.0bn, adjusted basic EPS R$10.80-11.40, low end targeted; cost of risk to high-teens by YE2026), bull/bear axes.
